name: timber

name: plant_fibre
note: bulked plant fibre; brush and cordage stock, the only thing available to bind with before metal

name: haft_blank
note: a riven haft, before assembly: the same timber, one process later

name: knapped_edge
note: a worked stone edge: flaked, not ground, which is what the stone age actually did

name: cord
note: twisted fibre; the first thing in the world that binds two other things together

name: hatchet
note: the edge is the part that identifies it, so the table reads it as the stone it is made of — a tool of two materials presents as the one that says what it does; the density is composed from the tool's own parts (a chert head and a timber haft at 70/100 and 30/100 by mass) as `corpus.rs` declares, giving 2.03 g/mL
no_consumer: a tool is held and used, not consumed by a process: what consumes it is wear, which is the MAINTAIN half of phase 3 and not a row in this rung

name: timber_offcuts
note: declared, not hoped for: a process that loses mass silently is a process that creates it
no_consumer: an end product: offcuts leave the process and accumulate. They are mass the ledger can still point at, which is why a loss is declared as an output rather than subtracted from the total

name: stone_flakes
note: knapping loses more than half its stone as flakes, and the ratio is declared in the process row
no_consumer: an end product: debitage. Salvage (Q71) is where it earns a consumer

name: fibre_dust
note: short fibres too fine to twist
no_consumer: an end product: short fibres too fine to twist

name: trim_waste
note: declared as `soil` because a mixture of stone, timber and fibre reads as aggregate
no_consumer: an end product: mixed-material trimmings, and the one declared destination for a process whose losses are not one material

name: forage
note: what a person can pick and eat: greens, berries and roots, taken from a forage patch by hand; the first consumer of the `edible` tag is somebody's hunger
no_consumer: eaten by a person, which is a need rather than a process row (Q51): the metabolism that would make it a process — food in, body mass and waste out — is the coupling phase 7 owns

name: charcoal
note: carbonised wood: the fuel of the ages before coal, and the first thing a kiln makes; its yield from timber is declared [D] because the charcoal-yield row in SOURCES.md is [NS]

name: brick
note: fired clay, and the first substance in the world that a fire makes rather than a hand
no_consumer: laid by a build, not by a process row: the first brick wall is a bill of materials a task plans, which is the sim's business rather than this table's. The process that would consume it — laying a fired wall — needs a mortar, and mortar needs the lime row SOURCES.md has not sourced yet

name: ash
note: the mineral part of wood and charcoal, which does not burn; declared at 1 % of the wood by mass for charring and 2.5 % for charcoal [D], and the density is the loose bulk figure
no_consumer: an end product: what a fire leaves that is still solid. It is mass the ledger can point at, which is the whole reason a burn declares it rather than rounding the loss away
